title: Grants for Melbourne Beach
lead: The town has budgeted $33,000 this year for grant writing (FY2027 budget, PDF p. 33). Below: grant programs that match records on this site. Matching is by County Commons; check eligibility with the agency.

fits.text: Florida DEP’s Indian River Lagoon water quality grants pay for stormwater and septic-to-sewer work; this year’s round is closed. Federal BRIC money (up to 75%) pays for drainage that lowers flood damage; Florida’s notices of interest closed August 14. The county’s Save Our Indian River Lagoon sales tax is up for renewal on November 3.

src.label: Florida Division of Emergency Management — BRIC

fits.text: Resilient Florida pays for projects that protect critical assets, but only after a town finishes a vulnerability assessment. The 2026 window closed September 1.

fits.need: Parks, the pier and the boat ramp
fits.text: FRDAP park grants of up to $200,000 close October 15, 2026. FIND’s Waterways Assistance Program pays up to 50–75% of boat ramp, pier and shoreline work, with applications due by the end of March.

No state road grant open to a town this size was confirmed. The $5.0 million bond on the November 3 ballot is the town’s own plan for roads and stormwater; this site gives facts on it and takes no side.

not_available: Florida’s Small County Outreach Program is for counties of about 200,000 people or fewer; Brevard is larger.
Florida’s Rural Infrastructure Fund is for rural communities; Melbourne Beach doesn’t qualify as rural.

already.text: A $6,000 safety grant from the Florida Municipal Insurance Trust, in this year’s General Fund.
The School Board pays back $77,000 for the school resource officer.
$101,371 of FEMA and state FEMA money arrived in FY2026.
